    Published: 05:58 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:41 EST, 23 November 2026.

    Mauricio Pochettino hauled his beleaguered Man United stars back into Carrington early on Monday morning after the newly introduced manager's chastening Anfield bow on Sunday.

    Pochettino, who replaced Michael Carrick last week, was served a sobering reality check at the hands of United's fierce rivals Liverpool, with the Red Devils on the receiving end of a 4-0 trouncing on Merseyside.

    The Argentine bemoaned the impact of what he described as a harsh red card against defender Leny Yoro in the opening eight minutes of the contest, but admitted he has plenty to do to turn things around - with United stuck in 19th in the Premier League table.

    And Pochettino had his players check in for training early on Monday morning, with a downcast Bruno Fernandes and his team-mates spotted arriving at around 8.30am - roughly an hour earlier than under Carrick.

    Under Carrick's stewardship, players were given the day after a game off, and it remains to be seen whether Pochettino will do away with that approach in favour of a recovery day at the club's training ground - a similar approach to that taken by former United boss Ruben Amorim.

    Man United stars were ordered back into training on Monday after their trouncing at Anfield.

    Matthijs de Ligt cut a contemplative figure as he drove through the gates at Carrington.

    Director of football Jason Wilcox continues to have questions to answer after Man United were unable to elevate themselves out of the relegation zone.

    News also came on Monday that Man United are appealing to the FA over Yoro’s controversial red card.

    Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free kick as 10-man United were thrashed 4-0.

    However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

    The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

    In September, Pro Ref boss Howard Webb apologised to United when Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand after VAR incorrectly ruled that teammate Enzo Fernandez was not interfering with play as he tried to head the ball in an offside position.

    Last season, Webb acknowledged that the match officials got it wrong when they decided not to send off Brentford captain Nathan Collins for hauling back Bryan Mbeumo inside the box as United lost 3-1 at the Gtech Community Stadium.

    Upcoming United head coach Pochettino blamed Yoro’s red card for the heavy defeat in his first game in charge, and was unhappy that Barrott took no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty area moments earlier.

    'So painful, so disappointed,' said the Argentine. 'It's not OK to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after eight minutes. Now we can explain everything, but the damage is done – it's so painful.

    It has been revealed that 'It's clear that after eight minutes the blueprint was in the bin. Do you think that is easy? Even the best team in the world playing in this situation concedes four goals or maybe more.

    It has been revealed that 'We are not going to lose more than one game how we lost today. I take the responsibility, and we keep pushing.

    'We feel pain for this defeat, but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger into energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game.

    Industry observers note that 'We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing-room.

    It has been revealed that 'The players are feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

    'We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.'.

    But more critical were former Red Devils Roy Keane and Gary Neville, both of whom were pushed to extremes assessing the match after the final whistle.

    Lisandro Martinez was among the Man United defenders that Gary Neville did not feel were up to the task at Anfield.

    But incoming manager Pochettino was keen to place the majority of blame on the harsh red card doled out to Leny Yoro.

    Neville was driven to slapping his face in the Sky Sports studio to demonstrate Man United's defenders' lack of hunger and poise.

    'I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here', he said before pointing to his head.

    'I never see any of them look like that,' he added. 'They look like that -'.

    Neville then stared into the middle distance for a few moments to share the blankness he sees on the faces of the back line, before spitting: 'Wake up!'.

    The Overlap broadcaster slapped himself a number of times while repeating 'wake up!' and adding: 'You play for Man United'.

    Keane was pushed to the brink of swearing in his snap description of the team's performance, adding that he thought Neville's verdict - that the 4-0 scoreline might have been worse under the circumstances - took players off the hook.

    'If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you're down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?' Keane stated immediately after the final whistle. 'It can be done.

    'I thought United were desperate. I thought they were so bad and everyone and Nev, who played for Man United saying 4-0 ain't bad.'.

    '(The red card) doesn't help but you're telling me they couldn't have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that's not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality - I can't believe what I'm hearing from people.

    In a recent development, 'You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn't too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can't believe what I'm watching sometimes.

    In a recent development, 'This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

    Recent findings suggest that 'When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'.

    Directeur général adjoint de l'ASSE en charge de la marque, du marketing et de la communication, Cédric Chambaz s'exprime dans le hors série de Décideurs Corporate Finances. Extraits.

    According to recent reports, "Il y a un changement macroéconomique dans l’industrie du football. L’ère du chef d’entreprise qui veut s’offrir une danseuse en investissant ses fonds propres pour se faire plaisir le week-end est derrière nous. Aujourd’hui, nous sommes dans une logique d’investissement beaucoup plus raisonnée, même si elle laisse toute sa place à la passion. Quand Larry Tannenbaum mandate Ivan Gazidis pour trouver un club de football dans lequel investir, il recherche un actif à fort potentiel sur un marché mûr. Il ne s’agit donc pas du tout de mécénat à fonds perdus. Pour autant, cet investissement porte sur un produit d’émotion, et l’AS Saint-Étienne dispose d’atouts considérables en la matière.

    Industry observers note that nous sommes un club patrimonial, une institution du football européen. Historiquement, nous sommes une des équipes les plus titrées de France et nous bénéficions d’un engouement qui dépasse largement notre territoire. Nos supporters sont répartis dans toute la France et notre fréquentation au stade est totalement décorrélée de notre niveau sportif actuel. Nous affichons la sixième affluence du football français, alors que nous évoluons sportivement en deuxième division.

    Pour Kilmer Sport Ventures, l’ASSE présentait des caractéristiques intéressantes mais le club était aussi une sorte de géant endormi qui, ces dernières années, n’avait pas bénéficié des investissements de modernisation nécessaires pour rester compétitif dans le football contemporain. L’idée est donc de réveiller le club grâce à des investissements ciblés, fondés sur une analyse approfondie de l’existant et de nos objectifs afin de repositionner l’AS Saint-Étienne comme une institution, sur le terrain comme en dehors.

    It has been revealed that un club de football peut être considéré comme un média. Plus son exposition est forte, dans les médias traditionnels comme sur les réseaux sociaux, plus il peut valoriser son inventaire commercial, c’est-à-dire les espaces qu’il propose à ses sponsors. À l’ASSE, nous bénéficions d’une audience nationale élevée. C’est ce qui nous rend attractifs pour le diffuseur, même en Ligue 2. Nous travaillons aussi à valoriser cette audience sur les réseaux sociaux, où nous rassemblons plus de 2,9 millions de fans sur l’ensemble de nos plateformes.

    Industry observers note that aujourd’hui, nous sommes capables de générer en France l’une des 10 plus fortes valorisations médiatiques pour nos annonceurs, et ce malgré notre présence en deuxième division. C’est notamment le fruit du travail mené en communication et en marketing pour faire rayonner l’équipe au-delà du stade.

    In a recent development, L’enjeu, au-delà de la seule billetterie, est de transformer notre notoriété en revenus. Cela passe d’abord par notre ancrage régional. Nous devons continuer à attirer des supporters au stade et à remplir Geoffroy-Guichard. Mais nous devons aussi toucher ceux qui ne peuvent pas venir au stade, en développant notre marque et nos produits dérivés. Cela suppose de travailler notre présence sur les réseaux sociaux, de valoriser les joueurs et de construire leur image, notamment lorsqu’ils sont issus de notre centre de formation. Certains disposent déjà de communautés importantes, capables de contribuer à la vente de maillots et d’ouvrir de nouveaux marchés. À défaut, c’est au club de construire cette visibilité.

    Recent findings suggest that notre ambition est de conquérir de nouveaux publics, notamment en Europe, mais chaque chose en son temps. Notre audience dépasse aujourd’hui notre territoire régional, mais nous ne pouvons pas prétendre rivaliser aujourd’hui avec le PSG à l’échelle internationale. Cela passera d’abord par le retour en Ligue 1 et par des performances sportives à la hauteur de nos ambitions. C’est toute la complexité de notre activité. Nous pouvons bâtir une stratégie marketing solide et développer nos outils de fidélisation, mais les résultats sportifs restent déterminants. Si vous perdez cinq matchs de suite, la dynamique commerciale s’en ressent forcément. Le projet sportif reste le juge de paix, même si nous devons apprendre à développer nos revenus au-delà du seul résultat du week-end.

    Recent findings suggest that la grande différence entre être DAF ou CMO d’une start-up dans la tech et dans un club comme Saint-Etienne ? A mon sens, elle tient à l’attachement des supporters envers le club et à la manière dont il influence leur vie. Très peu d’entreprises peuvent se targuer de voir leur logo tatoué sur le corps d’un de leurs clients et, pourtant, c’est le cas de l’ASSE. En outre, lorsqu’on se promène dans la ville, tous les acteurs économiques et politiques ont un avis sur la situation du club. Dans une région industrielle en difficulté, cette proximité et l’intensité de cette relation sont primordiales pour rassembler la population. Cette intensité m’a vraiment surpris, par comparaison avec les autres entreprises où j’ai travaillé. Le club cristallise des espoirs, des projections de succès qui transcendent le football.".

    • Recent findings suggest that défenseur de Chelsea, 8e de Premier League à 12 points du leader Arsenal de son ex-acolyte stéphanois William Saliba (remis de sa blessure au dos et pressenti pour jouer son premier match de la saison ce dimanche lors du choc contre Manchester City), Wesley Fofana est revenu hier sur ses vertes années dans Zack en roue libre.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that défenseur de Chelsea, 8e de Premier League à 12 points du leader Arsenal de son ex-acolyte stéphanois William Saliba (remis de sa blessure au dos et pressenti pour jouer son premier match de la saison ce dimanche lors du choc contre Manchester City), Wesley Fofana est revenu hier sur ses vertes années dans Zack en roue libre. Extraits.

    In a recent development, "Je suis arrivé en 2014 à Saint-Etienne. J’ai découvert la région, les Stéphanois. Le Forez… qu’est-ce qu’il fait froid là-bas ! C’est dur, la ville c’est compliqué. Tu peux entendre beaucoup de personnes te dire qu’il n’y a rien à faire dans cette ville, que c’est moche, etc. Mais moi j’ai bien aimé Saint-Etienne ! C’est sûr qu’il n’y a pas grand-chose à faire, que tu ne vas pas t’amuser comme si t’étais à Lyon, à Paris ou à Marseille. Mais il y a un p’tit truc, une histoire de fou et tu t’attaches à cette ville. Franchement, j’ai vécu de belles années là-bas ! A Marseille, il y a tellement une histoire forte que quand tu vas parler avec les gens, ils sont fiers de te parler de la ville. C’est beau. Sainté, c’est un peu similaire. Avec le froid en plus mais franchement c’est une superbe ville.

    C’est le seul club qui est venu me chercher, Saint-Etienne. Je jouais dans un club très populaire à Marseille qui s'appelle le Sporting Club Air Bel, et il y avait tout le temps des recruteurs car c'est un club qui est connu pour sortir des joueurs pour conduire en centre de formation. J'ai fait beaucoup d'essais, dans presque tous les clubs de France, à part le PSG et les clubs dans le Nord. J’ai fait des essais à Montpellier, Nice, Monaco, Toulouse, Bordeaux, Marseille. J'ai même fait Auxerre. Lyon ? Non. Quand t'es petit, pour aller à Lyon, il faut savoir jouer au ballon. Moi, j'étais trop un boucher !

    La première fois que j'ai fait un essai à Saint-Etienne, ils ne m'ont pas pris à la base, ils m'ont dit, « on va te revoir », la fameuse phrase « On te rappellera. » Mais ils sont revenus me voir quand je jouais avec Air Bel, et ils m'ont refait faire un essai. Et après cet essai, ils m'ont dit :  « c'est bon, on va te garder ». Quand j’arrive là-bas, c'est compliqué. En fait, t'arrives et il y a des règles, des codes, des trucs que tu ne peux pas faire. Et moi, quand j'étais petit, c'était un peu : si je veux faire un truc, je veux le faire. Et d'où je viens, il n'y a pas réellement... Ce n'est pas qu'il n'y a pas de règles, parce que ce ne serait pas bien de dire qu'il n'y a pas de règles. Parce que j'ai été éduqué, j'ai eu une bonne éducation, mais ce n'est pas pareil. Les règles, tu peux les contourner. Pour nous, les règles, si on n'est pas d'accord avec la règle, on va la contourner. Un peu de filouterie, voilà.

    Sauf qu'au centre de formation, ça ne passe pas. Et après, t'arrives, t'es dans un centre avec d'autres jeunes, des gens de ton âge, des gens qui jouent à ta place. Et c'est un peu la « guerre » parce qu'il y a des gens qui jouent à ta place, mais toi, t'es là, tu les regardes, t'as envie de jouer. C'est la concurrence, c'est comme ça. Mais oui, c'était un peu compliqué. Surtout, je quittais Marseille, j'arrivais à Saint-Etienne. Au début, je me suis dit « Mais qu'est-ce que je fous ici ? Qu'est-ce que je vais faire dans cette ville de fous ? » Un truc tout bête, tu sors dehors, c'est où qu'on peut aller grailler, c'est où qu'on peut aller manger ? Tu regardes les grecs, les snacks, il n'y a rien qui va. Tu veux aller te faire couper les cheveux, il n'y a rien qui va. Mais après, petit à petit, tu trouves les petites adresses, les connexions et j’étais bien. Tu rencontres des Stéphanois là-bas, ils te disent « T'inquiète, va ici, va là ».

    Franchement, au centre de formation, il y avait du niveau. Je pense qu'il y avait des jeunes en U17, U19, même en réserve, qui étaient « destinés » à du très, très haut niveau, mais qui n'ont jamais réussi à aller le chercher. Après, les Stéphanois, ils sont très fiers et ils ont des grosses valeurs. C'est ça, surtout, qu'on nous a appris. La valeur que le club, il a dans la ville, ça, on le comprend très jeune. Parce que les gens de là-bas, ils vivaient un peu à travers le club. Quand ça gagne le week-end, ils sont très contents. Quand ça perd, ils sont un peu tristes. Et dans la ville, tu le ressens. Le centre de formation, ce n’est que des bons souvenirs. On a fait beaucoup de bêtises, les directeurs du centre voulaient notre peau plus d'une fois. On va dire qu'ils ont des anecdotes. C'est des super souvenirs et on avait de belles générations. Franchement, moi, j'ai connu 98-99, ma génération 2000, 2001, 2002. Franchement, il y a eu des gros joueurs qui sont sortis. Il y a eu de très, très beaux joueurs.

    Recent findings suggest that C’est là que j’ai connu William Saliba. On  joué ensemble de U17 jusqu'à U19. On a gagné la Gambardella ensemble. Ouais, j'allais en parler. Même si il n'a pas joué la finale, on a gagné la Gambardella parce qu'on a joué la compétition ensemble. Et après, on a joué pendant un an, un an et demi ensemble. Lui, il est monté très vite en pro. On a joué en pro ensemble. Avec William, c'est une belle histoire parce qu'on a commencé très, très jeunes et on s'est retrouvés en pro ensemble. On a grandi ensemble et on est toujours en contacts même si on joue dans des clubs rivaux. Je le connais par cœur, il me connait par cœur. C'est la famille. On n'a pas besoin de se parler tous les jours mais on va se parler de temps en temps. On va se parler et après, quand on se voit, il n'y a rien qui bouge. C’est beau qu’on ait gardé ça. Parce qu'au-delà du fait qu'on ait grandi ensemble, qu'on soit arrivé au « sommet » ensemble, on joue au même poste. Ça aurait pu affecter notre relation mais depuis jeune, ça n'a jamais touché notre relation. On n'a jamais été affecté par ça, par la concurrence. Même quand on est arrivé en pro, il y a eu beaucoup de trucs qui nous ont mis en compétition, etc. Mais nous, ça ne nous a jamais rien fait. On s'en foutait. Nous, on voulait jouer ensemble, on voulait s'amuser et on voulait le meilleur pour l'autre,.

    It has been revealed that quand tu gagnes la Gambardella, t'es un peu la meilleure équipe de jeunes de France. Donc, c'était déjà quelque chose d'incroyable. Au lendemain de notre sacre en Gambardella, on fait un tour d'honneur à Geoffroy-Guichard. Je n'ai jamais fait de banc en pro à ce moment-là, rien ! On fait un tour d'honneur et trois semaines après, je suis sur le banc et il y a une blessure. Et le coach se retourne vers moi et il me fait rentrer arrière-droit contre Alain Saint-Maximin. La première chose que tu as en tête, c'est « il va me salir ». Parce qu'Allan, il est connu pour dribbler, pour salir les gens. Mais après, franchement, sur le moment, je rentre et moi, j'ai qu'un truc en tête, je me dis que chaque fois qu'il touche la balle, il faut que je le monte en l'air. Juste avant de rentrer, je vois l’entraîneur de Nice Patrick Vieira qui fait un geste demandant à ses joueurs d’attaquer de mon côté. Ça te met une petite bouffée de pression. Mais mon coach - enfin, c'était l'adjoint à ce moment-là -  m’a glissé deux ou trois mots avant de rentrer. Julien Sablé m’a dit : « tu joue simple, agressif, tu n’inventes rien , fais ce que tu sais faire. Tu castagnes, tu te bats, tu mets des tacles, des tampons. ». Je n’avais que ça en tête, simple, agressif. Ça s'est bien passé. Bon match, 3-0, première entrée, clean sheet.

    J’enchaîne la semaine d'après, c'est le dernier match de la saison, à Angers. Ma première titu. C’était facile car il n'y avait plus rien à jouer pour les deux équipes. C’était un super match, j’ai kiffé. C'était Jean-Louis Gasset, le coach. Tout le monde le connaît, c'est un mec simple. Et c'était une personne incroyable. J'ai appris beaucoup, beaucoup avec lui et avec son staff. Je n’en garde que de bons souvenirs. C'est sûr que je ne l'ai pas connu aussi longtemps que je l'aurais espéré parce que je n'étais pas réellement avec les pros. Je m'entraînais, mais je n'étais pas réellement avec eux. Ma première apparition en pro j’ai joué latéral mais franchement, je déteste ce poste. Après, comme je l'ai toujours dit, en vrai, tu ne décides pas trop. Tu vas jouer, surtout à cet âge-là, où on va te mettre. Qu'est-ce que tu veux dire ? Tu joues en pro, c’est déjà bien. Sois content, joue tes matchs, fais ton job et après, tu verras. Après, quand tu auras acquis de l'expérience, que  tu auras joué des matchs, tu pourras dire « moi, je préfère, je préfère ci, je préfère ça ». Quand tu es jeune, tu joues où on te met. On m'aurait même mis à gauche ou gardien, c'est bon, j’y serais allé.

    Je ne l'avais pas en moi, cette qualité de relance mais ça compte, surtout dans le football de maintenant. Ça compte de fou, ça compte énormément. Jouer au ballon, je n'avais pas ça en moi. C'est mon coach, Julien Sablé, que j'ai eu à Saint-Etienne qui m’a fait travailler ça. C'est lui qui m'a rendu fou et qui a pris des heures et des heures avec moi à me dire qu'il faut que la passe soit comme ça, qu'elle soit claquée, qu'il faut jouer dans ces intervalles-là. C'est lui qui m'a expliqué tout ça. Moi, à la base, moi, en tant que défenseur, mon job, et vraiment, j'ai grandi comme ça, c'était : « tu défends, te ne prends pas de but. On s'en fout à qui tu fais la passe. Quand tu as la balle dans les pieds, tu donnes à ton 6, ton arrière-droit. Ils se débrouillent. Eux, c'est leur job de faire le jeu, de s'amuser avec le ballon. » Moi mon plaisir c'était les tampons, les tacles, gagner mes duels, notamment de la tête. Et c'est après, petit à petit, en faisant des séances, des vidéos, etc., en prenant du temps sur le terrain, petit à petit que j'ai commencé à apprécier cet aspect du foot avec le ballon, et j'ai compris beaucoup de choses.

    J’ai fait ma première année en pro dans une équipe qui subissait et prenait beaucoup de buts. Tu subis beaucoup, donc tu défends beaucoup, tu es beaucoup exposé. En tant que défenseur, quand tu es jeune et que tu es beaucoup exposé et que tu défends beaucoup, on parle plus de toi, on te voit plus. Par exemple, on allait plus parler de moi qu'on allait parler des attaquants. Parce qu'on ne faisait que défendre et qu’on ne marquait pas beaucoup de buts. Et même quand on en prenait des buts, c'était souvent, « heureusement qu'il est là, sinon on en aurait pris plus ». Mais d'un autre côté, quand tu es défenseur et que ton équipe prend beaucoup de buts, tu passes des mauvais matchs, tu passes des mauvaises soirées. Tu vas jouer à l'extérieur, tu rentres chez toi, t'en as pris trois. Domicile, le week-end d'après, tu reçois, t'es as pris deux. Tu enchaînes les défaites, t’en prends 4, tu perds 5-1. C'est chaud, ce n'est pas un plaisir. Mais d'un autre côté, quand tu n'en prends pas, c'est multiplié fois 20 comparé à d'autres défenseurs ou à d'autres équipes du championnat. Franchement, c'était dur. Mais d'un autre côté, vu que tu défends beaucoup, tu es exposé pour un défenseur et à mon âge, c'était tout bénef pour moi.

    In a recent development, je fais cette finale de Coupe de France contre le PSG. Je fais un très bon match, mais malheureusement on perd la finale. Après cette finale, il y a un peu tout qui s'accélère. Il y a beaucoup de clubs qui s’intéressent à moi. Franchement, Leicester n’était pas là au début. Pour dire la vérité, à la base, moi, c'est Milan AC. Il y a un appel avec les dirigeants, avec Maldini. Maldini, c'est stylé. Quand il te parle et te dit « je vais te prendre sous mon aile » , j’ai envie de lui dire  « emmène-moi, je signe ce que tu veux. » Au départ, avec mes agents et tout mon entourage, on penche plutôt pour le Milan AC.

    Sources indicate that après, ça ne se fait pas avec Saint-Etienne parce que d'un côté, Saint-Etienne ne voulait pas me vendre. Mais d'un autre côté, ils étaient un peu dans l'obligation de me vendre par rapport à des problèmes d'argent, etc. Ils étaient un peu entre deux. Ils essaient un peu de faire remonter les enchères. On sait comment ça marche. Milan a monté jusqu'à une limite où ils ont dit « Ça ne sera plus possible. » Et il y a Leicester qui s'est ramené. Leicester, ça a été tout droit. J'ai parlé avec le coach, j'ai parlé avec Kolo Touré qui était dans le staff. Son discours m’a rassuré et mis en confiance. Ensuite, ce n’était pas compliqué. Leicester a fait une offre. Saint-Etienne était d'accord, mais après il y a eu ce problème avec Claude Puel, qui ne voulait vraiment pas me vendre. Mais au final, pour la santé du club, pour le bien du club, il n'avait pas trop le choix. Donc j’ai filé à Leicester l’avant-dernier jour du mercato.".

    Ian Holloway has been sacked by Swindon just two days after attempting to confront angry fans following defeat to Newport on Saturday.

    The journeyman manager had himself called the 2-0 loss on the road 'unforgivable' after he was taunted by home supporters chanting that he would be 'sacked in the morning' after the result.

    Holloway had intended to go down the tunnel after the final whistle, and passed the away stand on his route out, taking off his cap as he held up his hands in resignation.

    But as boos rained down on him, the 63-year-old could not resist the urge to engage, looking to answer back to the fans before he was restrained by security.

    Last month, Holloway described himself as a 'dead man walking' with the Robins mired 17th in League Two, but Monday morning saw him despatched after two seasons in charge.

    'Since joining the club towards the end of 2024, Ian has played an important role in stabilising our on-field position and helping the club make progress season upon season,' the Swindon statement announcing his departure read.

    Saturdays eh.#STFC pic.twitter.com/1GL3blApwW.

    Ian Holloway was caught up in a clash with fans after Swindon's defeat to Newport County - shortly before he was sacked (Source: X/Loathed Stranger).

    The journeyman manager oversaw two seasons at the club, saving them from relegation in 2024-25.

    'However, following careful consideration of recent results and performances, the club believes that now is the right time to take a different direction.

    'This has not been an easy decision, but the board firmly believes that it is crucial to make difficult decisions when necessary, always with the best interests of Swindon Town at heart.'.

    Holloway cut a disillusioned figure at Rodney Parade as he gave a heartfelt assessment of his side's performance after defeat to the Exiles.

    'It's devastating,' mentioned Holloway. 'I'm bitterly disappointed. Did I expect my team to do that? Not in a million years.

    'We're getting regular mistakes from almost everyone in that backline and in that midfield. We knew what type of game it was going to be. There's no excuses. I've just said to them "what on Earth do you think you're doing?" To start that way? It was so passive it was unforgivable.

    'It's very painful at the minute. It'll come back at the manager in the end if I listen to all these people (from the stands).

    Sources indicate that 'This is football. I've been in it a long time. This is my life.'.

    Holloway also questioned the desire of his players, continuing: 'Bitterly disappointed in all of them and disappointed for the fans. I get it, that didn't look like our team.

    It has been revealed that 'They scored two ugly goals. All our chances that we had, normally we take them.

    'Where's the fight? It's a local derby. I'm sorry, they've done their bits better than us.'.

    Holloway has endured an uneven stint at Swindon since 2024, saving the club from relegation in his first season but failing to challenge for the promotion places as time wore on.

    Memorably, the former Crystal Palace and Queen's Park Rangers manager claimed that the training ground was haunted shortly after his arrival in Wiltshire.

    Holloway had first suggested that there had been 'some strange things happening' after the club captain Ollie Clarke had ruptured his ankle in training, before enlisting his wife Kim to free spirits potentially trapped in the South West.

    'I'm absolutely devastated so I'm going to try and cleanse the training ground area because people are telling me it's haunted,' Holloway noted on BBC Radio Wiltshire in November 2024.

    Industry observers note that 'There's a graveyard somewhere near. Honestly, I'm not joking.

    'I think our training ground is very close to an ancient burial site so I'm going to get my wife to come up and say sorry to all these people and hopefully we'll have a bit more luck.'.

    Le trading constitue un levier essentiel de notre équilibre financier

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (450 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Poteaux-carres

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Directeur Général Adjoint de l'ASSE en charge des finances du club, Fabien Dawidowicz s'exprime dans le hors série de Décideurs Corporate Finances.
    • Industry observers note that "L'arrivée d’un actionnaire solide, ambitieux et passionné de sport comme Kilmer Sports Ventures constitue un atout.
    • Recent findings suggest that cette prise de participation s’articule autour de trois priorités.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Directeur Général Adjoint de l'ASSE en charge des finances du club, Fabien Dawidowicz s'exprime dans le hors série de Décideurs Corporate Finances. Extraits.

    Industry observers note that "L'arrivée d’un actionnaire solide, ambitieux et passionné de sport comme Kilmer Sports Ventures constitue un atout. Au-delà de sa dimension financière, il s’agit avant tout d’un investissement patrimonial, dans un club qui fait partie du patrimoine français, voire européen. L’AS Saint-Étienne bénéficie d’une résonance internationale, notamment grâce à son histoire et à ses parcours européens dans les années 1970.

    Recent findings suggest that cette prise de participation s’articule autour de trois priorités. La première concerne évidemment les équipes professionnelles, féminines comme masculines. La seconde porte sur les infrastructures, avec la volonté d’améliorer le centre d’entraînement et de poursuivre la modernisation du stade, en collaboration avec la Métropole de la ville. Enfin, le dernier axe, me semble crucial, car il reflète profondément l’ADN du club : c’est celui de la formation. L’académie doit permettre d’accompagner les jeunes aussi bien dans leur parcours footballistique que dans leur éducation afin de les préparer au mieux à une éventuelle carrière professionnelle.

    La baisse des droits télévisés ne signifie pas nécessairement qu’évoluer en Ligue 2 soit moins intéressant financièrement qu’en Ligue 1. Pour un club de Ligue 1 qui ne dispute pas de compétition européenne et se situe dans la deuxième partie du classement, les revenus audiovisuels peuvent être comparables à ceux d’un club de Ligue 2 de première partie de tableau, alors que les charges salariales sont généralement plus élevées dans l’élite. En échangeant récemment avec plusieurs directeurs administratifs et financiers de clubs de Ligue 1, nous avons constaté que les revenus audiovisuels d’un club classé dans le top 3 de Ligue 2 pouvaient être proches de ceux d’un club occupant la 15e place de Ligue 1.

    Sources indicate that L’enjeu est ailleurs. La Ligue 1 offre une meilleure valorisation des joueurs. Pour générer des revenus sur le marché des transferts, nous devons donc retrouver l’élite et y réaliser de bonnes performances. Cela vaut aussi bien pour les joueurs que nous recrutons et développons que pour ceux issus de notre centre de formation. Le trading de joueurs constitue ainsi un levier essentiel de notre équilibre financier.

    It has been revealed that en parallèle, nous devons optimiser nos coûts d’exploitation et mieux valoriser nos actifs. C’est tout l’intérêt des investissements dans les infrastructures, autour du stade comme au centre de formation. En offrant aux joueurs de meilleures conditions d’entraînement et de développement, nous augmentons leur potentiel de performance et, à terme, leur valeur sur le marché. Ces investissements doivent donc être considérés comme un moyen de renforcer notre capacité à générer des revenus futurs.".

    Il Torino farà debuttare la maglia celebrativa dei suoi 120 anni sabato 28 novembre alle 18:00, nella partita contro la Lazio al Grande Torino. Secondo quanto riportato da TuttoMercatoWeb, La divisa, realizzata con Joma per la stagione 2026/27, sarà prodotta in 1906 esemplari, ciascuno con un numero seriale sul fronte.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    Recent findings suggest that il club granata celebrerà l’anniversario il 3 dicembre anche con un allenamento a porte aperte allo stadio Olimpico. La società presenta così la nuova divisa: «Nella stagione del 120º anniversario del Club, Torino FC e Joma presentano una maglia speciale per la stagione 2026/27: un'edizione celebrativa che riprende alcuni segni dell'identità granata con uno sguardo rivolto al presente e all’innovazione».

    In a recent development, L’esordio in Torino-Lazio aprirà le iniziative legate alla ricorrenza. Nel comunicato, il club spiega: «La maglia celebrativa farà il suo esordio al Grande Torino sabato 28 novembre alle 18:00, in occasione di Torino-Lazio e darà il via alle iniziative che accompagneranno il Club fino a giovedì 3 dicembre e oltre».

    Il riferimento al Filadelfia e agli anni Ottanta accompagna il significato attribuito alla divisa: «Dal Filadelfia allo stadio, dagli anni Ottanta a oggi: questa maglia non chiede di guardare indietro, ma di celebrare le nostre radici nel presente. Ci ricorda che la Storia e la tradizione del Toro vivranno per sempre, grazie a chi continua a indossare questo colore e a tenere accesa la fede Granata».

    L’edizione è limitata a «soli 1906 pezzi», in richiamo all’anno di fondazione del Torino. Ogni esemplare porta il proprio numero seriale sul fronte. Sul granata acceso, sottili linee bianche riprendono la trama di una maglia da allenamento usata negli anni Ottanta al Filadelfia, dove si preparava la partita del fine settimana.

    Il comunicato descrive il passaggio di quella trama dal campo d’allenamento alla nuova divisa, reinterpretata in chiave contemporanea. Sulla maglia compare il toro rampante degli anni Ottanta, indicato dal club come un simbolo capace di unire generazioni diverse di tifosi attraverso i racconti e la passione di nonni e genitori.

    Una patch dorata dall’effetto cangiante celebra l’anniversario. Secondo la luce e il punto di vista, la scritta “Edizione limitata”, il logo e il numero 120 lasciano spazio al numero seriale del singolo capo. Lo stemma con il toro rampante è ricamato sul petto, all’altezza del cuore; il 120 ricompare sui bordi delle maniche, realizzati in tessuto elastico a coste. All’interno del colletto è stampata la data di fondazione: 3 dicembre 1906.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

    Recent findings suggest that their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

    It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

    But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

    According to recent reports, "That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

    Recent findings suggest that “Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”.

    Sources indicate that only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

    In a recent development, benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8.

    Recent findings suggest that united should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

    Industry observers note that yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

    “We’re bitterly disappointed,” stated Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”.

    It has been revealed that but clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

    Sources indicate that how had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

    Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their newly introduced sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

    It has been revealed that this is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

    The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

    Sources indicate that it could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

    United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

    When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

    His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

    According to recent reports, "That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia.

    “I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”.

    Industry observers note that they did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

    In a recent development, as Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

    Industry observers note that 2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq.

    It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

    Industry observers note that it’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

    I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

    Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

    Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

    Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

    Recent findings suggest that "That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

    According to recent reports, grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”.

The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

    Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

    #153394. Chambaz a gagné une invitation au Musée

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1179 w)
    📖 Baca

    Chambaz a gagné une invitation au Musée

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1179 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Poteaux-carres

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Directeur général adjoint de l'ASSE en charge de la marque, du marketing et de la communication, Cédric Chambaz s'est confié à Sportfin France.
    • "La nostalgie, c'est quelque chose qui est paralysant.
    • Le club de l'AS Saint-Etienne est une institution aujourd'hui parce qu'il était au pic de sa performance au moment où la télévision arrive dans les foyers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Directeur général adjoint de l'ASSE en charge de la marque, du marketing et de la communication, Cédric Chambaz s'est confié à Sportfin France. Extraits.

    "La nostalgie, c'est quelque chose qui est paralysant. Je préfère utiliser le terme d'héritage, et un héritage, on construit dessus, on ne peut pas renier qui on est. Ça, c'est un présupposé de base. On est un club de foot d'origine populaire qui s'est construit sur une région populaire avec une classe ouvrière très forte. Saint-Etienne, c'est une région qui était minière, qui avait une industrie sidérurgique développée, etc. et qui s'est développée autour de cette industrie. Une industrie qui a depuis périclité. On a un héritage, un héritage minier, un héritage ouvrier, et de ça, aujourd'hui, dans la marque, comme dans le comportement des employés, comme dans le comportement des joueurs, on a encore des traits qui sont très forts. Il y a cette valorisation de la notion de travail. Ici il est attendu, et on le voit dans les tribunes, nos ultras, n'ont de cesse que de le répéter, il faut mouiller le maillot. C'est une expression qui est devenue consacrée, qu'on utilise comme ça, mais les premiers joueurs de l'AS Saint-Etienne, c’étaient des gens qui sortaient de la mine et qui venaient jouer au foot. Pour eux, mouiller le maillot, ce n'était pas une image, c'était une vraie attente. Et aujourd'hui, on a cet héritage-là. Donc, aujourd'hui, oui, quand on regarde sur le passé, ça a créé quelque chose de fantastique.

    Le club de l'AS Saint-Etienne est une institution aujourd'hui parce qu'il était au pic de sa performance au moment où la télévision arrive dans les foyers. Donc, on est le club que tout le monde regarde à la télé, on devient la marque de football français qui plus en gagne. C'est à une époque où le football français n'avait pas gagné depuis des décennies. Alors, on gagne jusqu'à la finale à Glasgow contre le Bayern de Munich où les fameux poteaux carrés empêchent les Dominique Rocheteau, les Jean-Michel Larqué et Jacques Santini de remporter la Ligue des champions. Mais c'est une équipe qui domine, elle a 10 titres de champion de France dans cette période-là. Donc, on est le club de foot qu'on découvre à la télé, en même temps qu'on découvre à la télé. C'est un club qui gagne, donc on s'y associe et du coup, on établit une marque très très forte, un lien émotionnel très fort. Aujourd'hui, quand on dit les Verts, dans l'inconscient collectif de partout en France, c'est forcément Saint-Etienne. Il y a un lien très fort qui émane de là, donc on ne peut pas renier ce lien-là.

    Pour autant, il ne faut pas s'y enfermer parce que sinon, on n'est pas un club de foot, on est un musée. Or aujourd'hui, les ambitions du club, c'est de retrouver ce statut sportif et de faire en sorte que l'institution et sa performance sportive soient mises en corrélation. Aujourd'hui, il y a très peu de clubs qui sont dans cette adéquation. Le Paris Saint-Germain a réussi à aligner le statut du club avec sa performance sportive. Mais quand on est par exemple, en Angleterre, un pays que je connais bien, on a des institutions du football qui ont des vraies difficultés sportives. Et pourtant, ils restent des entités respectées, reconnues comme des clubs monolithiques dans lesquels on doit un respect, une reconnaissance. Je pense à Chelsea par exemple, qui a beaucoup de mal sportivement, ils n'ont pas gagné un titre depuis des années, et pourtant… Manchester United est dans le même acabit.

    Nous, on a cette ambition de valoriser cet héritage, de construire dessus, mais en se tournant vers l'avenir. Donc oui, on mettra en avant les Verts 76, on l'a fait l'année dernière pour le cinquantenaire de la finale de Glasgow, et on continuera de mettre en avant d'autres générations au fur et à mesure, parce que c'est sur leurs exploits qu'on a construit là où on est, mais on est définitivement tourné vers l'avenir plutôt que la glorification du passé.

    Recent findings suggest that du design à sa sortie, comment naît un maillot ? Déjà, c'est un travail collectif, dans lequel l'équipementier joue un rôle prépondérant. On a la chance, à l'AS Saint-Étienne, de travailler avec un équipementier qui s'appelle Hummel, avec lequel on a une relation de partenariat. Ce n'est pas toujours le cas, il y a certaines marques qui imposent au club « voilà votre maillot ». Nous, on a la chance d'être en partenariat avec Hummel et de travailler avec eux à la définition de ce maillot. Du coup, on est partie prenante du début jusqu'à la fin.

    C'est un process qui dure presque 18 mois. C'est-à-dire qu'aujourd'hui, on a des conversations sur les maillots pas de la saison prochaine mais de la saison d'après. On recherche, à l'AS Saint-Étienne, des designs qui soient à la fois respectueux des codes historiques, pour cette frange de nos fans qui sont très attachés aux valeurs traditionnelles du club. On cherche aussi à pousser les limites dans d'autres secteurs. Ce qui est sûr, c'est qu'on cherchera toujours à avoir un maillot qui soit portant de sens. Donc, on va faire des références à notre territoire, à nos supporters, au club.

    In a recent development, cette année, par exemple, le maillot 26-27 fait référence au premier titre de champion de France avec un design qui fait écho à celui de 1966-1967, quand le club est devenu pour la première fois champion de France, avec des bandes larges, un col blanc très large. Et quand on regarde le maillot de près, il y a un logo ASS Saint-Étienne [sic], irisé, qui apparaît, qui est le logo de l'époque. On a travaillé justement il y a un an et demi avec les designers de Hummel pour que ce produit, ce design, ce matériau soient celui-là, et que 18  mois plus tard, on puisse le révéler au public.

    C'est quelque chose qui dure 18 mois, une collaboration entre le club d'un côté, avec ses différents services, les personnes qui sont en charge de la commercialisation, qui ont un bon ressenti des produits qui vont se vendre, l'équipe marque qui va réfléchir à « est-ce que le produit enrichit la marque, fait référence à des éléments de la marque qu'on veut à soi ? », mais aussi la partie designer-produit plutôt chez Hummel. Et cette collaboration nous a permis de développer des produits qui répondent vraiment aux attentes de nos fans. Et on a vu une augmentation radicale du nombre de maillots qu'on a vendus. On a multiplié par trois nos volumes de maillots en cinq ans, grâce à cette collaboration prolifique avec Hummel.

    According to recent reports, cédric Chambaz vient donc de gagner une invitation au Musée des Verts. Il y découvrira que l'ASSE a en réalité décroché son premier titre de champion de France en 1956-1957. C'est à cette saison-là, magnifiée par la fameuse attaque mitraillette Rijvers-Mekhloufi, Njo Lea, que fait bien sûr référence le maillot porté par les protégés de Ian Cathro.

    Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

    Industry observers note that referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

    “It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

    One flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst said. “What do you do about that?”.

    Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

    The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

    On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

    Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

    Captain Luciano Valente noted the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

    “This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”.

    It has been revealed that van Bronckhorst said he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

    Industry observers note that “Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”.

    Bayern Munich slammed as 'despicable' and accused of 'co-ordinated' plot to undermine Jamal Musiala after club chief questioned star's contract due to his health concerns - with Jude Bellingham, Michael Olise and Rio Ferdinand backing the youngster

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1368 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 10:38 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 11:29 EST, 23 November 2026.
    • Bayern Munich have come under criticism from FIFA's players' union and leading figures in the game amid accusations that the club is attempting to slash Jamal Musiala's wages following his diagnosis with a 'neurological dysfunction'.
    • The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

    Published: 10:38 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 11:29 EST, 23 November 2026.

    Bayern Munich have come under criticism from FIFA's players' union and leading figures in the game amid accusations that the club is attempting to slash Jamal Musiala's wages following his diagnosis with a 'neurological dysfunction'.

    The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.

    Musiala shocked the sporting world when he collapsed in two matches earlier this season, with Bayern manager Vincent Kompany explaining that the player had suffered from a reaction to a change in his medication.

    Comments from members of Bayern's hierarchy have sparked controversy in Germany and abroad, with senior figures appearing to question the length of the player's contract – which runs until 2030 – should Musiala not recover his form.

    Honorary president Uli Hoeness was the first to speak out on the potential drop-off in form Musiala might suffer with long-term absences, claiming earlier this month that he 'may never regain the performance level he once had'.

    'We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,' Hoeness told German outlet BR24.

    Fifpro and international footballers have come out in support of Musiala over concerns that Bayern Munich might reduce his salary.

    Both Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have made comments suggesting consequences should Musiala not return to his level.

    Jan-Christian Dreesen also suggested that the club would need to 'assess' the situation if his performances do not return to their high heights.

    Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen then backed up Hoeness's comments and implied that Musiala's contract may need to be 'assessed'.

    Industry observers note that 'We're monitoring his level of play. He'll certainly need time to improve further – like any injured player,' Dreesen stated in discussion with AZ. 'And then we need to calmly assess the situation and, if necessary, sit down with his family and management.

    'Either we'll all be happy together and he'll be the same Jamal he always was – or, if he's a different Jamal along the way, we'll have to discuss it.'.

    Sources indicate that 'If we're not consistently at a level that also aligns with the economic realities, then we'll have to talk to each other. Nevertheless, we have a valid contract, and that's the end of it.'.

    The 23-year-old is one of Bayern's highest-earners, having signed a deal with the club to extend his time in Bavaria in February 2025. The deal is thought to be worth £18.4million per year.

    Adding fuel to the fire days later was former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who told Sky Sports/RTL that he thought it was almost reasonable to discuss a renegotiation should Musiala not return to the level at which he once played.

    'That is certainly possible and cannot be ruled out,' he stated. 'Unfortunately, what we know suggests that it will be difficult to reach the level that he has so often shown here in this stadium.'.

    It has been revealed that 'We need to talk to the family, the player, and above all, the agency. Because then these sums are – sorry, with all due respect – no longer feasible.

    Sources indicate that 'I can't imagine Jamal leaving the club or another club buying him under these circumstances. That's a problem. I think we handled this very sensitively with the player, and we're all interested in him coming back - ideally in top form. But what happens if that's not the case? Then we'll still have to think about the finances. And that's a task that the board and the supervisory board unfortunately have to make.'.

    Rummenigge added that he did not think it was 'problematic' for these discussions to be happening publicly, due to the club's interest in 'him coming back and playing well'.

    But the player union Fifpro were forthright in their disagreement with his statements,  releasing a statement claiming that all parties presently sharing their views on Musiala's contract 'should know better'.

    'Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession,' the statement read.

    'In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.'.

    When this statement was shared to social media via journalist Fabrizio Romano, global talents including Jude Bellingham and Musiala's team-mate Michael Olise were among those to like the post.

    Musiala collapsed on the pitch at two consecutive games in August (pictured being helped by team-mates against RB Leipzig).

    The 23-year-old has been diagnosed with absence seizures and is managing his medication.

    Vincent Kompany has been supportive of his player's struggles, and took him off the bench with some success last weekend.

    Rio Ferdinand elaborated on those comments in a more detailed post on social media, adding that he believed the club are 'better than this'.

    In a recent development, 'If they want to negotiate more reasonable terms for the club going forward due to the health challenges Jamal has, then surely speak to him and his team rather than to the media,' Ferdinand wrote on X. 'This situation must be hard enough to deal with for Jamal without the media and club officials talking about it publicly.

    Industry observers note that 'Bayern Munich are one of the clubs who from afar have always carried themselves with a class and standard that most have admired. Sadly, this just doesn't feel like Bayern Munich in this situation.'.

    Criticisms were even more fiery in Germany, with the vice president of Germany's player union Michael Franz accusing the club of harassment.

    Industry observers note that 'What the Bayern Munich officials are doing, and I don't mean Kompany and (Max) Eberl (director of sport), who have behaved impeccably, seems despicable to me,' Franz shared in an interview with Sport1. 'There is even something about it that resembles harassment.'.

    It has been revealed that 'A footballer's level of performance can be discussed publicly, but it is not right to talk about his illness and the salary he receives in such circumstances. We must not forget that Jamal Musiala has done everything in his power to come back.'.

    'Money has become more important than the person, and that is unacceptable.'.

    Former Bayern captain Stefan Effenberg stressed how crucial 'support and protection' from the club towards their players is, particularly for those in greater need like Musiala.

    'We are talking about someone who is suffering from an illness. What I would have expected is for the club's senior officials to apologise,' Effenberg remarked, adding that he thought that the communications from the club had been 'disastrous'.

    Musiala collapsed twice within four days in mid-August, first during Bayern's match against Leipzig – shortly after scoring – and then against Heidenheim.

    He then returned to the pitch in September, netting against Bodo/Glimt in Champions League action and Union Berlin shortly before the first international break.

    After suffering a hamstring injury, Musiala then spent time away from the side before his return at the end of last week – a match which also saw Harry Kane suffer an ankle injury which will keep him out for over three months.

    Fifpro's statement went on to add that Bayern must be careful with their player's mental wellbeing as well as his physical challenges.

    In a recent development, 'Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala,' the statement continued. 'Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

    It has been revealed that 'Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

    'Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.'.

    Il centrocampista ripercorre i prestiti a Cagliari ed Empoli e ricorda il derby vinto e il gol di Provedel.

    Sources indicate that matias Vecino ripercorre il cammino dalla Fiorentina alla Lazio: i prestiti a Cagliari ed Empoli, il lavoro con Maurizio Sarri e quella che definisce una «seconda giovinezza» in biancoceleste. Secondo quanto riportato da Gianlucadimarzio, Dopo tredici anni di calcio italiano, tra esperienze, incontri e traguardi, il centrocampista è in attesa di un nuovo capitolo.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    In a recent development, intervistato da Gianlucadimarzio.com, Vecino parte dal suo arrivo dall’Uruguay nel 2013. Aveva grandi aspettative, ma anche qualche timore per ciò che avrebbe trovato in Italia.

    «È stato un salto molto grande», racconta Vecino. «Da un lato ero felicissimo, dall’altro avevo un po’ di ansia perché non sapevo cosa avrei trovato.» L’inserimento fu più semplice di quanto immaginasse grazie ai compagni e alle persone che lavoravano nel club. Tra coloro che lo aiutarono ricorda Borja Valero, Gonzalo Rodriguez e Neto: era ancora un ragazzo, con molto da imparare.

    Recent findings suggest that il debutto in Italia arrivò il 26 settembre 2013, a San Siro, durante Inter-Fiorentina. Era già stato in panchina nelle partite precedenti, senza entrare in campo. L’emozione coinvolse anche la sua famiglia, che lo seguiva dall’Uruguay. Giocare in quello stadio contro calciatori come Cambiasso e Milito gli diede la sensazione di essere un giocatore vero. Durante l’azione restava concentrato, ma quando il pallone usciva poteva guardarsi attorno e sentire l’importanza del momento.

    Recent findings suggest that per trovare spazio in Serie A, Vecino passò in prestito al Cagliari e all’Empoli. Alla Fiorentina giocava in una squadra importante, ma le occasioni erano limitate: considera quelle due esperienze una scelta giusta per accumulare minuti.

    In a recent development, in Sardegna trovò Diego Lopez, uruguaiano come lui, in una squadra che aveva bisogno di una mezzala. A Empoli lavorò con Sarri, in un gruppo con molti giovani. Ricorda un campionato in cui la squadra giocò molto bene e si divertì, in un ambiente familiare. Fu la sua prima stagione intera da titolare: «tatticamente mi ha migliorato al 100%», dice a proposito del tecnico.

    Dopo due anni in prestito tornò alla Fiorentina, con cui raccolse 78 presenze in due anni. Tornare in viola era sempre stato il suo obiettivo: il club lo aveva preso dall’Uruguay e aspettato, e lui desiderava costruirvi un percorso lungo. Il rientro coincise con l’arrivo di Paulo Sousa. Vecino ricorda una squadra forte nel primo anno e il divertimento dei tifosi, ma ritiene che alla lunga abbia pesato l’impegno in Europa League.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 12:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:02 EST, 23 November 2026.
    • Chelsea are lurching towards a crisis after yet another loss in which they were bullied, this time by Leeds United.
    • That 4-1 hiding saw Xabi Alonso heckled, and his players booed at both half-time and full-time, arguably deservedly so for such a disastrous showing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

    Published: 12:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:02 EST, 23 November 2026.

    Chelsea are lurching towards a crisis after yet another loss in which they were bullied, this time by Leeds United.

    That 4-1 hiding saw Xabi Alonso heckled, and his players booed at both half-time and full-time, arguably deservedly so for such a disastrous showing.

    It has led to tentative speculation around Alonso's future as Chelsea prepare to travel to Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest on Friday night, not to mention questions about where he is going wrong and how he might arrest his team's slump in form.

    Here, Daily Mail Sport tackles all the burning issues at Stamford Bridge...

    Chief among Chelsea’s problems is the fact they have conceded 20 Premier League goals this season. It is as many as they have scored at the other end. So, as much as we have enjoyed their freescoring forward line this season, so too must we criticise their disastrous defending.

    We know Alonso can organise a defence. His Bayer Leverkusen side only conceded 24 goals when they won the Bundesliga as unbeaten champions in 2023-24. Chelsea are now on the verge of overtaking that total before we even hit December.

    Liam Delap, their former striker now at Forest, will be desperate to add to that tally this Friday, too.

    Xabi Alonso is coming under growing pressure, with his Chelsea side failing to back up their promising early-season form.

    Levi Colwill was all at sea against Leeds as Chelsea shipped another four goals, taking their tally to 20 in 11 games.

    According to recent reports, this morning, I watched back all 20 of the goals that Chelsea have leaked this term. There have been so many individual mistakes.

    It has been revealed that like on day one, in the 3-2 win at Fulham, when an out of position Robert Sanchez let in Josh King's shot. And when Levi Colwill missed a defensive header which should have been routine, which led to Gonzalo Garcia scoring.

    Chelsea got rid of Sanchez after that game, but Emiliano Martinez has hardly helped shore up this defence, as was apparent in the 4-1 loss to Leeds, when Colwill and Co were again all over the shop.

    Until they cut out the silly mistakes, it is hard to see Chelsea competing at the top end of the Premier League.

    Industry observers note that every manager at every club is sackable. Nobody is immune. But that’s not to say Alonso is suddenly up for the chop at Chelsea. I haven’t heard anything which would suggest those inside the club think finding a fourth permanent manager in the year 2026 is the answer.

    According to recent reports, let’s not forget the overwhelming optimism when news broke of Chelsea striking an agreement to hire Alonso. It was an hour or so after the club had lost the 2026 FA Cup final to Manchester City. Recently, I took a look at the comments section of the story I wrote that day. It was full of excitement from Chelsea fans, and anger from Liverpool supporters at missing out on him.

    In a recent development, anyway, I think it’s too soon for us to start talking about Alonso’s job. He is in a bad moment, obviously. A very bad moment. Losing at home to Tottenham Hotspur and Leeds is a complete no-no for any Blues boss.

    The supporters are more likely to curse his name than chant it right now, and it is hard to identify the style Alonso wants, with few discernible patterns of play to Chelsea's football.

    But let’s give the bloke a chance to get himself out of this jam as he heads into his 12th Premier League match.

    Sources indicate that believe it or not, Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it. Enzo Maresca resigned, exiting on January 1, 2026. Liam Rosenior was sacked, yes, but the club were effectively forced into that change as the players clearly gave up on him. Let’s see if Alonso can find some solutions.

    Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it and Alonso, remember, has only had 11 Premier League games in charge.

    We’ve tried to coax a little anger out of Alonso at press conferences, practically encouraging him to have a pop at his players for how they are performing, but he tends to resist the urge.

    He’s clearly a nice guy. However, a Chelsea source does tell me he’s different behind the scenes. We may not see it on the outside, but internally, he is perfectly capable of being fiery with the players.

    Which I hope is the case. Because sometimes, it can feel as if these Chelsea players need a good kick up the backside, rather than being coddled.

    It has been revealed that I wrote a piece after the 4-1 loss to Leeds about how superstars can be stroppy. It’s normal. They can be so good that when the game isn’t going their way, they show their sulky side.

    Recent findings suggest that palmer did that both during and after Saturday’s defeat. It was pretty poor from him to not want to go around applauding the fans who had bothered to stick around at full-time, even if there had been boos. An apology has been attributed to Palmer on social media, but that’s just another case of fake quotes being circulated.

    It has been revealed that for me, Palmer has to look at himself as much as anybody. It’s been too long since we’ve seen him try to take a match by the scruff of the neck.

    Cole Palmer put in another quiet display against Leeds - he needs to start taking matches by the scruff of the neck.

    WHAT HAPPENED WITH EMEGHA AFTER THE GAME?

    It has been revealed that striker Emmanuel Emegha started for the first time and scored for the first time in Chelsea’s 4-1 loss to Leeds. Then he exited Stamford Bridge.

    We have seen players leaving the stadium on foot before. Videos of Palmer being surrounded by supporters while being escorted to his ride home occasionally crop up on social media.

    Sources indicate that emegha had possessions stolen from his car while he was in a restaurant after the match and the incident has been reported to police. He was not harmed.

    From a footballing point of view, I'd like to see Emegha start away at Forest this Friday.

    According to recent reports, not that I’m aware. He’s been linked with Paris Saint-Germain and I had an email from a PR person this morning trying to push a loan to AC Milan or Roma as a possibility.

    According to recent reports, alonso has given the fans what they wanted in the last few league games. He started Estevao against Manchester United, brought him on at half-time at Sunderland and started him against Leeds.

    Estevao, clearly an exciting talent, could do with taking these opportunities to show why he deserves more of them.

    Estevao has been given a chance to shine by Alonso in recent weeks but has failed to grab his opportunities.

    I could see Malo Gusto leaving if there’s interest and Chelsea don’t keep demanding £75million, because it is hard to see who would spend that on him.

    Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign. Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in the loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

    I wouldn’t be surprised if a few other fringe players are linked with leaving in pursuit of game time ahead of January, such as Valentin Barco and Jamie Gittens, who is training again after his ankle injury.

    As for incomings, I don’t need to tell you that Chelsea are interested in Alex Scott of Bournemouth. Arsenal are, too, but the word is the Blues are still the frontrunners as we approach January. Whether Scott is what this team needs is another conversation.

    See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

    PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

    PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

    Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

    Recent findings suggest that PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

    But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

    The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

    It has been revealed that team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

    Sources indicate that “We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”.

    The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a newly introduced feature PortuGOAL will be bringing you some recommended reading about Portuguese football from around the web, penned by our own network of writers or others.

    We kick off by alerting you to a superb interview in the Guardian by Nick Ames with Port Vale's Portuguese manager Bruno Ribeiro. The headline writer focused on Ribeiro's relationship with José Mourinho, but it is the detail of Ribeiro's struggle to make things work at an English third-tier team of meagre resources that makes for fascinating insight.

    Benfica are top of the Liga NOS and their coach Rui Vitória continues to confound the doubters who believed he would not be up to the job at the Lisbon giants. Simon Curtis takes a look at "the quiet man at the helm of a national institution". And Benfica fans, while we've got your attention, a shout out for Tom Kundert's profile of the club's world-renowned Seixal Academy for ESPN.

    Talking about Portuguese football schools, none has produced more top-class players in recent decades than Sporting's Alcochete Academy, and the excellent Outside of the Boot website has a brilliantly detailed profile written by Mateus Carvalho of another possible gem for the Lions, Francisco Geraldes, who is currently on loan at Moreirense.

    To finish up this initial trip around the net, we alert you to FourFourTwo's list of the 59 best Under-21 footballers from around the world. The section we highlight has a mini profile of Porto striker André Silva, who will be hoping to net his first senior international goal tonight for the Seleção against Andorra. In case you're wondering, the British magazine rank him at number 23.
